2. Heard Ms. Mandvi Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.295 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 326A,
304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kankarkhera, District Meerut, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

She has nothing to do with the said Sushila Devi vs State Of U.P. on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71778329/

sentences.text: There is dying declaration of the deceased person, whereby it is alleged that her husband had forcibly administered some chemical, which was poisonous.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated thatthere is no allegation against the applicant, rather the said dying declaration mentions that the applicant and her sister-in-law used to live separately to the husband wife duo.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 13.06.2025 and she is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. The Supreme Court in the judgment ofKahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, (2022)
6 SCC 599has categorically opined that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text:
ofKahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, (2022)
6 SCC 599has
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.
8. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

9. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
10.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
11.

The Supreme Court in Jalaluddin Khan Vs. Union of India, (2024) 10 SCC 574, held that 'bail is the rule, jail is the exception' even in special statutes like the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act,
1967.

entities.text: Jalaluddin Khan Vs. Union of India, (2024) 10 SCC 574
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the conditions in the special statute for the grant of bail are met, then bail should be granted.
12. Learned A.G.A./State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
13. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A./State Law Officer.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the dying declaration of the deceased person and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Sushila Devi, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
16. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

17. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
